subject: Store Management
examFormat: Two papers combined in a composite paper taken at one sitting. Paper 1 has fifty multiple-choice questions lasting 1 hour for 50 marks. Paper 2 has seven essay questions of which candidates answer any five in 2 hours for 100 marks.
excluded: The source text omits the number and heading of topic 7 (listed as Record Keeping because its content is documentation, source and trade documents).

subtopics.name: Store Management
objectives: Explain the meaning and importance of store management
State the functions and characteristics of a store manager
Explain customer services: pre-sale services and after-sale services

subtopics.name: Functions of Management
objectives: Explain planning, organization, leading, staffing and controlling

subtopics.name: Factors to be considered in establishing a store
objectives: Identify the factors to be considered in establishing a store: market, finance, types of stock, transport, accessibility, security, government regulation and personnel

subtopics.name: Retailing
objectives: Define retailing
State the functions of a retailer

subtopics.name: Wholesaling
objectives: Define wholesaling
State the functions of a wholesaler

subtopics.name: Warehousing
objectives: Explain the meaning, types and importance of warehousing

subtopics.name: Transportation
objectives: Define transportation
Identify the means of transportation and state the advantages and disadvantages of each
State the factors that determine the choice of transport

subtopics.name: Introduction to Stock Control
objectives: Explain the meaning and importance of stock control
Identify the types of stock records: stock list, bin card/store card, store requisition form and delivery notes

subtopics.name: Methods of Stock Control
objectives: Describe the manual method: periodic, perpetual and annual stock taking
Describe the computerized method
Explain the levels of stock control: maximum level, minimum level and reorder level
Explain the issuing of stock: FIFO and LIFO

subtopics.name: Pricing
objectives: Define pricing
Identify the types of pricing: skimming, mark-up, mark-down, penetration, and below or above mark pricing

subtopics.name: Organizational Policy Statements
objectives: Define organizational policy
Explain employment policy
Explain decisions on customer services and public relations

subtopics.name: Organizational Standards
objectives: Define standards
Explain productivity standards
Explain standards for customer's satisfaction

subtopics.name: Organizational Culture
objectives: Define culture
Explain organizational culture: attitude to customers, relationship with co-workers, relationship with the boss and dress code

subtopics.name: Overview of Communication
objectives: Define communication
Identify the types of communication: oral, written and non-verbal
Identify business documents: letters, memos, reports and circulars

subtopics.name: Electronic Communication
objectives: Define communication
Identify the means of communication: fax, telephone, email and radio messages
Use word processing: use a computer to write a business letter

subtopics.name: Overview of Basic Business Law
objectives: Define business law

subtopics.name: Law of contract
objectives: Explain the elements of contract
State the rights and obligations of employer and employee

subtopics.name: Agency
objectives: Define agency
Identify the types of agents
Explain the creation of agency
State the rights and obligations of principals and agents

subtopics.name: Sale of Goods Act
objectives: Explain the contract of sale
Explain the formalities of sale

subtopics.name: Government Regulation of Business
objectives: Explain the meaning and uses of patent right, copy right and trade mark
Explain the Health and Safety at Work Act, consumer protection agency and licence

subtopics.name: Government Regulatory Agencies
objectives: Identify the roles of government regulatory agencies: NAFDAC, NDLEA and SON

subtopics.name: Documentation
objectives: Define filing and indexing
State the rules of filing
Describe filing and indexing methods

subtopics.name: Source document
objectives: Explain the meaning and types of source documents: invoice, receipts, cheques and vouchers

subtopics.name: Trade Documents
objectives: Identify documents used in foreign trade: bills of lading, certificate of origin, consular invoice, insurance certificate, inspection certificate, bill of exchange, indent, letter of credit and proforma invoice
Identify documents used in home trade: order, enquiry, waybill, consignment note, manifest, invoice, proforma invoice, receipts, credit and debit notes and vouchers

subtopics.name: Subsidiary Books
objectives: Explain the meaning, types and uses of subsidiary books: purchase and sales day books, returns outwards/inwards books and cash books

subtopics.name: Imprest System
objectives: Define and describe the imprest system
Prepare a petty cash book

subtopics.name: Final Accounts
objectives: Define final accounts and state their purpose
Prepare a simple Trading, Profit and Loss Account and Balance Sheet

subtopics.name: Sales / Turnover
objectives: Explain the meaning of sales/turnover
Calculate the rate of sales turnover

topics.name: Risk Management
objectives: Define risk management
Describe the methods of risk management: sound management practices, reduction of risks (optimum stock level), hedging and risk transfer through insurance

subtopics.name: Investments
objectives: Explain the meaning of investment and of capital investment
Explain investment in the capital market
State the functions of the Stock Exchange
State the advantages of share holding
Explain money market instruments: meaning, treasury bill, commercial papers and bonds

subtopics.name: Taxation
objectives: Explain the meaning and importance of tax
Identify the types of tax: income tax, import duties, excise duties and VAT
